answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a proof-of-attestation mechanism that requires endorsements from established peers. Each new identity must secure a unique sponsorship from a cedar tree farmer who stakes 10% of their annual yield, amounting to $100. This identity then submits original work, graded by peers from a karst community, who assess the quality each. As more fake identities are created, costs increase; each additional sponsor raises the total stake required, like adding a plume to a taxidermy collection, where every feather comes with its own hefty price tag.
